final_idea.motivation: The primary goal of this experiment is to enhance the flux-pinning properties of EuBCO films by introducing BYNO as artificial pinning centers (APCs) through pulsed laser deposition (PLD), aiming to improve critical current density (Jc) and pinning force density (Fp) at low temperatures and high magnetic fields.

strategies.tuning strategies: Doping EuBCO with BYNO to form nanorods as APCs, which significantly enhance Jc by providing strong pinning centers in high magnetic fields.
Utilizing hot-wall PLD to ensure stable heating during deposition, improving longitudinal critical current (Ic) uniformity and reproducibility.
Depositing EuBCO on IBAD-MgO substrates with a CeO2 buffer layer to provide a well-aligned template for epitaxial growth, enhancing superconducting properties.
Adjusting the deposition rate during PLD to control the orientation and density of BYNO nanorods, reducing anisotropy and improving Jc across various magnetic field angles.

Optimizing the thickness of the EuBCO layer through deposition rate control to balance Jc at 77 K and self-field with in-field Ic values at 4.2 K, making it suitable for high-field magnet applications.

final_idea.technique: The fabrication of BYNO-doped EuBCO films utilizes hot-wall pulsed laser deposition (PLD), an advanced technique for high-rate deposition of thick superconducting films. Sample characterization employs transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to observe nanorod and nanoparticle structures. In-field critical current (Ic) and Jc measurements are conducted using a four-probe transport method with high-field superconducting magnets, providing precise data on flux-pinning properties. The use of photolithography and wet etching to form microbridges is a standard but critical technique for accurate Ic measurements.
final_idea.outcome: For high-field magnet applications (e.g., NMR, cryogen-free superconducting magnets). Critical current density (Jc) 1.5-3 times higher than pure EuBCO at 4.2 K and ≥ 3 T; Pinning force density (Fp) > 1.0 TN/m3 at 4.2 K; Critical current (Ic) up to 464 A for FAST sample at 77.3 K, self-field.
